releases.notes:
First stable release of the Heidrun Hotline protocol package.

Ships `HeidrunCore` (wire types + Network.framework client), `HeidrunNIOClient` (cross-platform SwiftNIO client), and the `heidrun` CLI.

Capabilities negotiated via `DATA_CAPABILITIES` (0x01F0):
- **Large-file transfers (>4 GiB)** — 64-bit sizes, 24-byte HTXF handshake, 64-bit FFO fork headers; single-file and folder.
- **UTF-8 text encoding** — opt-in UTF-8 for all strings (chat, names, news, …); macOS Roman otherwise.

Plus Heidrun extensions (0xE000 band): emoji avatars, resource-fork framed downloads. Self-signed TLS, tracker registration/listing, news, file transfers.

The wire format is additive and backward-compatible: every extension degrades gracefully against peers that don't negotiate it. See docs/PROTOCOL-EXTENSIONS.md.

releases.title: heidrun-protocol 1.0.0-rc24
releases.notes:
First tagged GitHub release for **heidrun-protocol**. Notes span the recent admin line (rc22 → rc24); the headline is **over-the-wire administration** — the cross-platform NIO client and the `heidrun` CLI both gained full admin powers.

The package ships three products, pure Swift 6, macOS + Linux:

- **`HeidrunCore`** — Hotline wire format, value types, codecs, the Network.framework `HotlineNetworkClient`, and the tracker client.
- **`HeidrunNIOClient`** — cross-platform Hotline transport on SwiftNIO.
- **`heidrun`** — text-only Hotline CLI ("modern HX") built on `HeidrunNIOClient`.

---

## 🔑 Over-the-wire admin on `HeidrunNIOClient`  (rc22)

The SwiftNIO client gained the six account-admin transactions, byte-for-byte mirroring the Network.framework client: `createLogin`, `deleteLogin`, `openLogin`, `modifyLogin`, `kick` (with optional ban), and `broadcast`. This is what unblocks cross-platform (Linux) administration. Wire quirks honoured: `openLogin` (TX 352) sends the login **plain** while every other auth/admin transaction XOR-obfuscates it; `modifyLogin` password is tri-state (`nil` omits, `""` sends a single `0x00`, non-empty obfuscates); privilege bytes match the classic bitfield.

---

## 🖥 `heidrun` CLI admin surface  (rc23)

The CLI exposes those operations two ways, sharing one set of tested argument parsers:

**REPL slash commands** (need the matching server privileges):

```
/newuser <login> <pass> <nick> [priv,…]
/getuser <login>
/moduser <login> <nick> [priv,…] [pass]
/deluser <login>
/kick <socket> [ban]
/broadcast <message>
```

**One-shot scripting flags** — connect, do one operation, exit with a status code (non-zero on a usage or server error), no REPL:

```bash
heidrun <host> -l admin -p <pw> --create-user bob secret Bob readChat,sendChat
heidrun <host> -l admin -p <pw> --modify-user bob Bobby readChat --user-password newpass
heidrun <host> -l admin -p <pw> --kick 5 --ban
heidrun <host> -l admin -p <pw> --broadcast "back in 5"
heidrun <host> -l admin -p <pw> --delete-user bob
```

Privileges are comma-separated **names** (e.g. `readChat,sendChat,postNews`), backed by a new public `PrivilegeNames` name↔bit helper in `HeidrunCore` (40 named bits).

---

## 🆕 Discoverability + versioning  (rc24)

- **`/version`** (`/ver`) — prints the CLI version **and** the negotiated protocol versions (client advertises vN, server reports vN). `//version` still asks the server for its own version string, so nothing is lost.
- **`/privs`** (`/privileges`) — lists the valid privilege names in the REPL, so you don't have to read source or crib off `/getuser`.
- **`heidrun --version`** and **`heidrun --list-privileges`** — both work **offline** (no `<server>` argument needed).
- Version source of truth: `HeidrunProtocolInfo.version` in `HeidrunCore`.

---

## Pinning

Pre-release tags compare lexically, so pin with `exact:`, never `from:`:

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/franckjej/heidrun-protocol.git", exact: "1.0.0-rc24")
```

GPL-2.0. No breaking API changes — additive throughout.
